title: Functional Components
summary: Functional components are JavaScript functions that return React elements. They are the primary way to build UI in modern React. A component name must start with an uppercase letter so React distinguishes it from HTML tags. Components can be composed — a parent renders child components just like HTML elements. Each component should ideally do one thing (single responsibility).
keyPoints: A component is a function that returns JSX (React elements)
Component names must start with an uppercase letter: App, Header, MovieCard
Components are reusable — use them like custom HTML tags: <MovieCard />
Compose components: a parent renders children, building a tree
Each component should have a single responsibility
Export components to use them in other files: export default function App() {}
Components re-render when their state or props change

exercises.prompt: Which is a valid React functional component?
exercises.explanation: A functional component is a function that returns JSX. The name must start with an uppercase letter so React treats it as a component, not an HTML element.

exercises.prompt: Why must component names start with an uppercase letter?
options: It is a JavaScript language requirement
React uses the casing to distinguish components from HTML elements
Uppercase names run faster in the virtual DOM
It is only a convention — lowercase works too
exercises.answer: React uses the casing to distinguish components from HTML elements
exercises.explanation: React treats lowercase tags as HTML elements (<div>, <span>) and uppercase tags as components (<MovieCard>, <Header>). A lowercase component name would be rendered as an unknown HTML element.

exercises.prompt: How do you use a MovieCard component inside another component?
exercises.explanation: Components are used like HTML tags in JSX: <MovieCard />. Calling them as regular functions works technically but bypasses React's rendering lifecycle.

options: An error — variables cannot be used in JSX
exercises.explanation: The curly braces {} embed the JavaScript variable name into the JSX output. The rendered result shows the value of the variable.

exercises.prompt: Which is the correct way to export a component for use in other files?
exercises.explanation: ES module syntax (export default) is the standard way to export React components. module.exports is CommonJS and not typically used in React projects.

options: Combining CSS styles from multiple components
Building complex UIs by nesting components inside other components
Merging multiple components into a single function
Inheriting behavior from a parent component class
exercises.answer: Building complex UIs by nesting components inside other components
exercises.explanation: Composition means a parent component renders child components in its JSX, forming a tree. This is React's primary pattern for building UIs — prefer composition over inheritance.
